questions.text: Let (H.,) be a subgroup of G and a,b ∈ G . Let Ha and Hb be two right cosets of H in G. Then prove that the two right cosets have the same number of elements .
Determine the number of strings of length 20 that can be formed using A, B, C, if it must contain at least two A’s and at least two C’s.
Define a distributive lattice and show that in a distributive lattice (L, ≤), if a ∧ x = a ∧ y and a ∨ x = a ∨ y for some a in L, then x = y.
Let E(x1,x2,x3,x4) = (x1^x2^x3')V(x1^x2'^x4)V(x2^x3'^x4') be a Boolean expression over a 2-valued Boolean algebra {0,1}. Write Boolean expression both in CNF and DNF.
Show that the number of partitions of a positive integer n in which no part occurs k or more times is equal to the number of partitions of n in which no part is a multiple of k.
Let G be a group, H a cyclic subgroup of G, and g ∈ G. Let K = {gHg¹| h ∈ H}. Show that K is also a cyclic subgroup of G. Also show that if H has order n, then K also has order n.
Find the shortest path from B to all other vertices for the network given in the diagram below using Dijkstra’s Algorithm.
In a Boolean lattice (L, ≤) with a, b, c ∈ L, prove that: (i) a ∧ (b ∨ c) = (a ∧ b) ∨ (a ∧ c) (ii) a ∨ (b ∧ c) = (a ∨ b) ∧ (a ∨ c)
Prove that a graph is bipartite if and only if all its cycles are even
Find the 83rd and 103rd permutations of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in both lexicographical and Fike’s order.
Let G = {...}. Show that G forms a group under matrix multiplication. Is G Abelian? Justify.
Show that .... is a tautology.
Let (H.,) and (K,.) be subgroups of a group (G,.). Define HK = {hk| h ∈ H, k ∈ K}. Prove that (HK,.) is a subgroup of G if and only if HK = KH.
Prove that any self-complementary graph has 4n or 4n+1 vertices, where n is a non-negative integer
Give an arguement which will establish the validity of the following interference: All integers are rational numbers. Some integers are powers of 2. Therefore some rational numbers are powers of 2.
Draw any two self-complementary graphs with 5 vertices and find the diameter of those graphs.
Prove that a graph G is a tree if and only if between every pair of vertices there exist a unique path.

Let G = R − {−1} (R is the set of real numbers). Define * on G as a * b = a + b + ab. Then show that (G, *) forms a group. Is G Abelian? Justify your answer.
Show that Z₅ = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} forms a cyclic group under the operation addition modulo 5. List all the generators of Z₅.
Prove that a nonempty subset H of a group (G, *) is a subgroup of G if and only if a * b⁻¹ ∈ H for every a, b ∈ H
If repetition is not allowed, how many four-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8. How many of the numbers are less than 4000?
How many ways are there to distribute 27 identical jellybeans among three children (a) Without restrictions (b) With each child getting at least 5 beans
For any a, b, c, d in a lattice (A, ≤), if a ≤ b and c ≤ d then show that a ∨ c ≤ b ∨ d and a ∧ c ≤ b ∧ d.
Let E(x₁, x₂, x₃) = (x₁ ∧ x₂)' ∨ ((x₁ ∧ x₃)' ∨ x₂) be a Boolean expression over the two-valued Boolean algebra. Write E(x₁, x₂, x₃) in both DNF and CNF.

Find the following permutations for n = 5 with initial permutation 12345: (i) 90th permutation in lexicographical order (ii) 90th permutation in reverse lexicographical order (iii) 100th permutation in Fike's order.

Consider the following premises: If there was a ball game, then travelling was difficult. If they arrived on time, then travelling was not difficult. They arrived on time. Using propositional inference theory, show that there was no ball game
Prove that (∃x)(P(x) ∧ Q(x)) ⇒ (∃x)P(x) ∧ (∃x)Q(x).
Let (L, ≤) be a distributive lattice. Prove that for any elements x, y ∈ L, if a ∨ x = a ∨ y and a ∧ x = a ∧ y for some a ∈ L, then x = y.
